name: log10x
description: Ranks log patterns by volume and cost and plans compact (Splunk, self-managed Elasticsearch), tier down or offload to S3 for the excess over each cap. The MCP server runs on the machine the agent runs on, over stdio, and no log data reaches log10x.

interface.longDescription: Log10x ranks the log patterns that drive a log platform's bill by volume and cost, and plans compact (Splunk, self-managed Elasticsearch), tier down or offload to S3 for the excess over each cap. On Datadog and CloudWatch the levers are tier down and offload. Without an account the server starts read-only against the public Log10x demo dataset. With an account key it queries the account's per-pattern metrics. The MCP server runs on the machine the agent runs on, over stdio, started with npx and pinned to one release, and no log data reaches log10x. The tool that writes engine policy needs an account and runs only when the agent asks to apply, subject to the client's approval prompt. For the engineers who own log costs on Splunk, Datadog, Elasticsearch, ClickHouse or CloudWatch.
capabilities: Rank log patterns by volume and cost
Write engine policy with an account
defaultPrompt: Which log patterns drive my log cost?
Show me how to install Log10x on my stack.
Which action applies to my top pattern on Splunk?
